_meta.purpose: Ground truth labels for turn detection clips. Update all numeric fields after recording each clip — current values are estimates based on the suggested text length.

fields.text: exact words spoken in the recording
fields.user_started_at_s: timestamp where the first word begins — detected via silence analysis, 0.0 if speech starts immediately
fields.overall_class: finished | unfinished | wait — the final disposition of the whole utterance
fields.user_finished_at_s: timestamp where the last word ends. null if overall_class is unfinished and recording was cut
fields.pauses: array of mid-sentence silence intervals; each has start_s, end_s, correct_label
fields.notes: free text — what this clip is testing

_meta.labeling_tip: open each clip in Audacity or any audio app, use the timeline to read seconds, round to nearest 0.1s

clip-01.wav.text: I want to book a flight to Bangalore for next Tuesday morning.
clip-01.wav.notes: clean delivery, no mid-sentence pauses — sanity check that both approaches predict 'finished' correctly here

clip-02.wav.text: I want to book a flight to ...um.. Bangalore for next Tuesday.
clip-02.wav.notes: single mid-sentence pause after 'flight to' (~1.3s long) — primary baseline-vs-smart test case

clip-03.wav.text: Hmm I think ... I. aaa. want a window seat please.
clip-03.wav.notes: thinking pause — tests whether the smart system handles disfluencies (Hmm, I think) and the pause that follows

clip-04.wav.notes: single-word turn — tests that the system doesn't wait for more after a clearly complete one-word reply

clip-05.wav.notes: short utterance, no pauses, falling intonation

clip-06.wav.text: What was the price for the morning flight you mentioned earlier?
clip-06.wav.notes: question form, rising intonation at end — checks the LLM treats questions as 'finished'

clip-07.wav.text: Cancel my booking ... actually wait ... change it to evening instead.
clip-07.wav.notes: two mid-sentence pauses, user reconsiders mid-utterance. Tricky: the word 'wait' appears mid-sentence but is NOT the wait-class — that's about the whole utterance's intent, not isolated words

clip-08.wav.notes: very short single-word turn — stress test for any system that requires minimum speech duration

clip-09.wav.text: Bhai matlab I want to .un... book a flight to Mumbai.
clip-09.wav.notes: code-switched (Hindi+English) with a mid-sentence pause — tests ASR robustness to mixing AND pause handling together

clip-10.wav.notes: proper noun risk — ASR may hear 'book mark' (two words) instead of 'bookmark' (one word). Affects whether the LLM sees the right transcript

clip-11.wav.text: So I was thinking about my travel plans for next month and I really want to visit ..un. maybe.. Bangalore or Hyderabad ... I haven't decided yet ... but I'd like to book something soon if possible.
clip-11.wav.notes: long monologue (15-20s) with 3 mid-sentence pauses — biggest test of the smart approach. Baseline will likely cut at the first pause. Adjust pause timestamps after recording

clip-12.wav.notes: fast quick turn, no pauses, clear sentence-end intonation

clip-13.wav.notes: wait-class — grammatically complete but agent must NOT reply. This is the clip that justifies the 3-class taxonomy. A binary system would predict 'finished' here and incorrectly respond
